subject: Migration mode selection follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@nova.health>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@nova.health>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Migration mode selection follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Samir / Elena,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through Nova Health's current inference setup and constraints. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can align on deployment mode (Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private/VPC or on-prem).

Key notes from today:
- Current environment: self-hosted LLM endpoints on legacy GPU cluster (NVIDIA V100 nodes), EC2-based model runtime, internal model ops.
- Primary drivers: PHI compliance, data residency (US-only), predictable latency for patient-facing features, and cost predictability for large batch workloads.
- Traffic profile: ~150k requests/day today, spike to ~450k on weekdays; typical request size ~300 tokens; tail latency SLO target 250ms for single-turn queries.
- Pain points: frequent infra ops, model upgrades break inference performance, and no autoscaling for burst traffic.

Recommendation (initial): 
- Given PHI and residency needs, Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool with VPC peering) or Redwood Private (managed private control plane or on-prem package) are the frontrunners. Hosted API would be fastest to trial, but would need the Private path for production PHI workloads unless covered by BAAs and VPC options.

Attachments: I attached a short proposal for Dedicated vs Private that outlines the tradeoffs and a migration playbook (redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf, redwood-migration-playbook.docx). Also attached our latest SOC 2 report for compliance review (soc2-report-2026.pdf).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether Nova will require an on-prem deployment (air-gapped) or if a VPC-only Private install is acceptable?
2) If VPC is acceptable, we'd like to schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (solutions engineer) to review network/firewall constraints and peak throughput testing — suggested slots: Wed 07/07 or Thu 07/08, 10:00-11:00 PT.
3) Please share an infra diagram or list of egress/IP controls we should be aware of (if possible via Drive link).

Thanks — happy to adjust timing.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Khan <samir@nova.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nova.health>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock in the deep-dive: 

1) PHI: We will need a BAA and evidence of SOC 2 and encryption-at-rest + in-transit. The SOC2 you attached looks good; we'll need a short summary of how Redwood's Private option handles key management (KMS/HSM) and whether keys can be customer-managed.
2) Throughput/latency: The 250ms SLO is for a 300-token median request. Our current infra struggles at spikes — can you share typical instance sizing you'd recommend for our peak of ~450k/day with 10 req/s sustained and 200 req/s burst across regions?
3) Migration path: We're currently on a combination of other LLM APIs and self-hosted models. We need a plan to migrate traffic incrementally (canary + A/B) and a fallback plan back to prior endpoints during rollout. Any references/process for re-routing at the API layer would be helpful.

We can do Wed 07/07 at 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. I've attached a short infra overview and network diagram (nova-infra-overview.pdf). Timeline-wise, target pilot in Q4 2027.

Samir
Director of ML Engineering | Nova Health
samir@nova.health | +1 (650) 555-9876

---
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@nova.health>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@nova.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Samir / Elena — thanks for the infra diagram, Samir. Quick answers to your questions and what we'll cover in the deep-dive: 

- BAA & KMS: Redwood can sign a BAA. For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS/HSM). For Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra in your VPC), we support customer KMS rotation and customer-controlled IAM roles. I'll bring our security SME to the call for detailed key-handling flows.

- Sizing & throughput: For your traffic profile (median 300 tokens, peak 200 req/s), a safe starting point is a 4x g4dn.12xlarge-equivalent GPU pool for Dedicated (NVIDIA A10/A100 equivalent depending on model), with autoscaling configured for burst capacity. Rough throughput: ~150-250 tokens/sec per A10-like GPU for standard llama-like models; this gets you headroom for 200 req/s bursts with batching and prefix caching. We'll propose a concrete baseline after reviewing exact model family and sequence-length distribution.

- Migration path: Redwood supports routing policies (canary, A/B, percent rollouts) at the API layer with automatic fallback to a previous model variant or an external endpoint. We'll send a short tech note during the call showing the routing policy JSON and an example mutual action plan.

Attachments: I'll upload a sample routing policy + quick sizing worksheet during the deep-dive. In the meantime, Marissa attached our Dedicated vs Private proposal and SOC2 report.

Next steps I suggest for the call (Wed 07/07 10:00 PT): 1) Walk through your infra diagram and egress/IP constraints; 2) Confirm model family and exact seq-len distribution; 3) Validate KMS/BAA questions with security contact; 4) Agree on pilot scope and success metrics.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@nova.health>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@nova.health>

Date: Fri, 08 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration mode selection follow-up - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks everyone — confirmed for Wed 07/07 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

Action items before the call: 
- Samir / Elena: please confirm whether customer-managed KMS is required for pilot (yes/no) and share any compliance contacts who need the SOC2 packet.
- Samir: if you can upload the full network ACLs or firewall egress rules to the Drive link I shared, that will speed validation.
- Dev / Dylan: prepare the routing policy sample, sizing worksheet, and a short note on on-prem packaging options and associated timelines.

I'll follow up after the call with an updated mutual action plan and a rough cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private (I included a draft proposal in the attachments). If Nova confirms on-prem is required, we'll scope the Private on-prem package and provide an SOW.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
